genZNote: The reason legumes don't need nitrogen fertilizer — it moves into root nodules and converts atmospheric N2 into a form the plant can use, rent-free (well, in exchange for sugar).

habitat.naturalHabitat: Soil, and root nodules of leguminous plants (peas, beans, lentils, clover)
habitat.hostAssociation: Symbiotic nitrogen-fixing partner of leguminous plants; not associated with humans or animals
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Widespread agricultural soil organism, host-specific to particular legume species/varieties

microscopy.appearance: Gram-negative rods; pleomorphic bacteroid forms inside nodules

culture.colonyMorphology: Circular, convex, translucent to white, often mucoid (gummy) colonies from exopolysaccharide production

identificationClues: Forms root nodules on specific host legumes, visible as small swellings on the root system
Converts inert atmospheric nitrogen (N2) into ammonia via the nitrogenase enzyme complex, a process requiring an oxygen-poor microenvironment inside the nodule
Mucoid, gummy colonies on yeast-mannitol agar from exopolysaccharide production
Host-specific — different Rhizobium species/biovars nodulate different legume hosts

examFacts.importantTest: Root nodule formation on host legumes; acetylene reduction assay for nitrogenase activity
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Classic biological nitrogen fixer, foundational to sustainable/legume agriculture
